chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Ibn Fudal, from Ali ibn 'Aqaba, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Then He accepted their repentance.» He said: It is pardoning.

key_terms.ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ: Then He accepted their repentance (Quranic phrase)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'Then He accepted their repentance' mean in Shia exegesis?
ai.summary: In this concise exegesis from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the divine acceptance of repentance in Surah At-Tawbah as *al-iqalah*, signifying Allah's gracious overlooking of sins rather than merely a formal pardon. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on Allah's mercy as an active, benevolent act of covering faults, reinforcing the concept that true repentance invites divine grace beyond simple forgiveness. The narration underscores the theological nuance that Allah's 'acceptance' is an act of magnanimity that restores the believer's standing with a sense of ease and relief.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hussein, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali bin ‘Aqaba, from his father, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
with regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Then He (accepted their repentance by) repenting upon them.» [9:118] He said: It is pardoning.
